The decisive mistake was the Orchestrator declaring the request satisfied at Step 28. It did so on an unverified Bing snippet. The daily price of $8.25 came from a third-party listing (visitacity.com), not the museum's official ticket page. The annual-pass prices came from another search snippet. The Orchestrator never had the museum's own ticket and membership pages checked, and it never confirmed the 2-year-old's admission rules. It then ended the run. The final calculation therefore dropped the 2-year-old and compared against the wrong inputs, giving -201 instead of 45.
